title: First Responder: Launch KPI Standup + Decision Grid
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable daily standup brief and decision grid for the First Responder launch team. The doc is intentionally compact so on-call/product-ops can run a 10–12 minute sync and make deterministic go/no-go or mitigation calls for the first 72 hours post-activation. Use this as the single source for who speaks to which KPI and the exact thresholds that escalate to action.

Standup rhythm (10–12 minutes):
1) Quick health snapshot (2 minutes) — ops lead posts: global RTT 95th, 5-min error rate, tail latency, and capacity utilization.
2) KPIs by owner (6 minutes) — each metric owner gives one-line status + recommended action if threshold crossed.
3) Decision & Actions (2–4 minutes) — trigger grid evaluated, actions assigned, immediate fixes dispatched.

Roles & owners (quick reference):
- Ops lead / facilitator: Miguel Torres — runs the standup, owns incident comms.
- Capacity & Autoscale: Priya Nair — monitors GPU pool fill, queue growth, autoscale alarms.
- Model Quality / Evals: Jonah Patel — monitors QA evals, sample regression checks.
- Customer Success escalation: Lea Morgan — handles high-priority customer threads and SLAs.

Primary KPIs, definition, and short thresholds: (owner)
- 5-min error rate: percent of failed requests over last 5m (Ops). Green <0.3%, Yellow 0.3–1.0%, Red >1.0%.
- 95th latency (generation): p95 token-to-token time for live model path (Ops). Green <250ms, Yellow 250–500ms, Red >500ms.
- Queue depth (requests waiting for batch): absolute count (Capacity). Green <50, Yellow 50–200, Red >200.
- Throughput (tokens/sec): aggregated tokens served (Capacity). Green at or above target throughput, Yellow -10% to -25%, Red >25% drop.
- Quality regression rate: percent of sampled responses flagged by evals (Model Quality). Green <0.5%, Yellow 0.5–1.5%, Red >1.5%.
- Cost burn variance: 24h spend vs expected per-day baseline (Finance/Product). Green within ±10%, Yellow 10–25% over, Red >25% over.

Decision grid (deterministic outcomes):
- Any Red in error rate OR p95 latency + Queue depth Red => immediate partial traffic diversion to fallback model & paging SRE.
- Quality regression Red (auto-eval) => rollback latest model rollout to previous pinned version, disable live rollout, notify customer success.
- Throughput Red with Queue depth Yellow => enable burst capacity and increase batch size (Capacity owner executes runbook).
- Cost burn Red but all performance green => temporary throttle non-critical routes, enable cost caps and notify finance.

Fast actions (playbook snippets):
- Divert traffic: runbook link (Confluence) — migrate 30% traffic to lower-cost model variant and monitor for 10 minutes.
- Rollback model: tag previous model in Console -> rollback -> verify sample set in prod-sample eval channel.
- Scale pool: Capacity CLI: increase reserved nodes by +2, enable burst; monitor queue reduction.

Incident triage priority (what to do in first 30 minutes):
P0: system-wide failures (error rate >3%) or data corruption — page on-call SRE, cut traffic to hosted fallback.
P1: severe latency/throughput regression impacting SLAs — enable burst, start canary rollback.
P2: isolated customer regressions — route to customer success and open P2 ticket.

Standup artifacts to update after call (owners):
- Ops lead: add one-line summary to Launch Command doc and update incident status.
- Capacity: update capacity burn table and queue chart.
- Model Quality: push failing sample IDs to eval dashboard and flag top 5 regressions.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Do we want automated traffic diversion at Queue depth >150 or keep manual? (decision needed by product before beta).
- Define which routes are "non-critical" for cost cap throttles — list to be finalized with growth.

Next steps / immediate wishlist:
- Convert grid into small Console widget for first 72h (owner: engineering solutions).
- Add a lightweight Slack alert that summarizes the 6 KPI lines into a single standup message.
- Run two dry-runs with simulated surge this sprint and validate decision timings.

Notes & history:
This doc was iterated from longer launch playbooks — distilled into a daily-first-responder checklist to reduce cognitive load during high-noise windows. Use as working doc and update thresholds after each major beta.
